title: PulseMonitor — Fire and Forget
objective: The uptime checker pings a URL and tells you nothing but 'done' — no status, no body, nothing. Prove you can still make it reach an internal-only service, blind.

verifier.condition: The simulated internal admin service's own side effect (a counter it increments) changes as a result of a request submitted through the blind checker, although the checker's response reveals nothing about what happened.

weakness: The server makes an outbound request to a user-supplied URL and discards everything about the result, so there is no direct read-back — but the request itself still reaches wherever it's pointed, which is enough to trigger a side effect on an internal service.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /check (url field; fetched server-side, response fully discarded)
seededData: A simulated internal admin service at internal-admin.lab:80 whose /ping-count path increments an in-memory counter on every request it receives.
hints: The checker's response is always the same no matter what you send it. Does that mean nothing happened on the server?
You can't read anything back directly here. Is there somewhere else in this application that might show the EFFECT of a request, even without showing its content?
This lab exposes a small internal status page for its own debugging. Check it before and after you try something.
burpNotes: Send a check request for a candidate internal URL, then separately fetch /__debug/ping-count to see whether it changed — the checker's own response will never tell you anything.
